Issued at 225 AM CDT Sat Oct 31 2026

We've seen a few patches of rain (and even a rumble of thunder or 
two!) move slowly north across southern MN through the night. This 
rain is moving in ahead of a pool of high theta-e air in the 925-
850mb layer coming up out of the Iowa. As this pool of low-level 
moisture moves north, it's running into an h5 ridge axis that 
extends from the southeast US, up into southwest MN and continuing 
on into Alberta. This combo of low level theta-e advection and upper 
ridging results in weak forcing and a setup that models have been 
really struggling to resolve where these little batches of showers 
pop-up. The general idea though as that we will see a band of 
scattered showers lift north through the morning, with showers 
cutting off from south to north this afternoon. For trick-or-
treaters, this rain will be pretty much done by the time we get to 
sunset, so you shouldn't need to add an umbrella to your kid's 
costumes. 

Going into Sunday, outside of an occasional sprinkle, we look dry. 
We also look to loose the low clouds, but should hold on to upper 
clouds. The NBM looks a little aggressive with the clearing it has 
for Sunday, but how much we clear out will determine how warm we get 
for the first day of November. If we clear out as much as the NBM 
indicates, then we'll see highs in the upper 50s in western MN, with 
mid 60s in eastern MN and western WI. If we stay mostly cloudy with 
mid/upper level cloud cover, then you can probably take about 5 
degrees off the highs we currently have for Sunday.

Next week looks to start on a very wet note. We continue to see some 
spread in the models with the track of a surface low Monday night 
into Tuesday, but there is a general consensus on this low moving 
across southern MN. The current NBM winds show a surface low going 
from roughly Canby to the Twin Cities Monday night, then slowly into 
northwest WI on Tuesday. PWATs with this system continue to run 
nearly off the charts for November, with the EPS mean values of 1.5" 
running about 4.5 standard deviations above normal. This high 
moisture content paired with a LLJ in excess of 50 kts will create 
zone of strong and very moist isentropic lift ahead of the low 
during the day on Monday, which will result a shield of moderate to 
heavy rain and embedded thunderstorms moving across the area, with a 
widespread 1-2" of rain expected with just this. Monday night, as 
the low moves into MN, we'll see this WAA precip transition to 
deformation precipitation within the cold conveyor belt (though the 
air in this cold conveyor belt is not November cold!). Tuesday 
afternoon, we'll also likely see another round of showers and 
thunderstorms develop ahead of this systems cold front from eastern 
MN into western WI. When all is said and done, some very anomalous 
rainfall amounts for November look likely. Where we double dip on 
the isentropic lift and deformation forcing north of the surface low 
track, a storm total of 2-3+" of rain still looks like with this 
storm. Given where the NBM currently shows the surface low track, 
these high end rain amounts look most likely from western into 
central MN. As for the severe weather potential; moisture, forcing, 
and shear will be ample, but instability, especially surface based, 
looks to be lacking. Not helping is the nocturnal timing for the 
surface low passage, but we could see some severe potential into 
western WI Tuesday afternoon depending on the timing of the front. 

How long this system lingers is a bit uncertain, with the NBM 
continuing to slowly step down PoPs through the day on Wednesday into 
Thursday given the timing/placement differences in the models. With 
that said, outside of the Canadian, models are trending toward rain 
ending in the MPX area Wednesday afternoon. After that, it's split 
flow and a very meh weather pattern for us. This will likely start 
another 1-2 week long period where we see little, if any 
precipitation, with temperatures continuing to run 5-10 degrees 
above normal. There are no signs of winter paying us a visit through 
the first half of November.
